resolvedFindings: Mission instructions use direct verbs and separate required actions from advanced behavior.
Incident language avoids sensational descriptions and unsupported guarantees of safety.
Agent, evidence, grounding, tool, handoff, human approval, and recovery match the campaign glossary.
Media narration does not rely on visual or audio information alone.
Canonical character and place names remain stable across participant, instructor, UI, and media surfaces.
French instructions use natural operational syntax rather than literal English sentence structure.
Élément probant, ancrage, outil, transfert, approbation humaine, and rétablissement follow the approved glossary.
Mission titles, public presentation labels, instructor controls, narration, and captions are localized.
Mission Control remains the named product surface while Port Azure and character names remain canonical.
Inclusive phrasing avoids unnecessary gender for units, participants, residents, and software agents.

reviews.reviewedBy: Operation Lighthouse Brazilian Portuguese localization review
resolvedFindings: Brazilian Portuguese instructions use natural operational language and inclusive plural constructions.
Agente, evidência, fundamentação, ferramenta, transferência, aprovação humana, and recuperação follow the approved glossary.
